intelligence_brief.title: Semiconductor Supply Chain and Critical Mineral Geopolitical Assessment

Taiwan.developments: TSMC continues to accelerate 2nm process node development despite escalating cross-strait military posturing. Supply chain diversification remains the primary strategic objective for major clients.
Taiwan.risk_assessment: Critical infrastructure remains vulnerable to potential maritime blockade scenarios.

Japan.developments: Rapid expansion of domestic foundry capacity via Rapidus and increased investment in advanced packaging facilities to secure regional supply chain resilience.
Japan.risk_assessment: Moderate; dependent on imported raw materials for photoresist and high-purity chemicals.

United_States.developments: CHIPS Act funding tranches are being finalized for major domestic fabrication projects. Export controls on high-end AI accelerators to China remain the primary geopolitical friction point.
United_States.risk_assessment: High; ongoing labor shortages in specialized engineering roles and environmental permitting delays.

Gallium_Germanium.developments: Export permit requirements from China continue to create price volatility and supply uncertainty for compound semiconductor manufacturers.
Gallium_Germanium.risk_assessment: Critical; limited alternative sourcing options in the short term.
